concepts.title: Temples as Living Architecture
concepts.definition: Indian temples are stone records of faith and craft - from the stepwell Rani ki Vav and the hill shrine of Hidimba Devi with its timber style to towering gopurams - each region developing its own temple architecture shaped by local material and worship.
concepts.key_idea: Temple architecture varies by region and material, but everywhere it joins devotion with engineering.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees203.txt lines 130-180 (Rani ki Vav, Hidimba Devi temple, Sharada Peeth temple)
question_patterns: describe the main features of Indian temple architecture

solution_steps.explain: Note the shrine, hall and tower that frame most temples.
Stone carving, timber work or stepwell architecture follows what the region offers.
Sculpture and space plan serve ritual and pilgrimage.

concepts.title: Mosques, Forts and Sultanate-Mughal Building
concepts.definition: The coming of Islamic architecture brought the arch, dome and minaret: grand mosques like the Jama Masjid of Delhi and Ahmedabad, along with forts and tombs, blended Persian ideas with Indian craftsmanship to create an Indo-Islamic style.
concepts.key_idea: Arch, dome and minaret met Indian carving to build the Indo-Islamic synthesis.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees203.txt lines 137-175 (Jama Masjid Ahmedabad, Jama Masjid Delhi)
question_patterns: what new elements did Islamic architecture bring to India

how did Indian craftsmen shape sultanate buildings

solution_steps.explain: Arches, domes and minarets mark the imported style.
Local stone, motifs and workmanship fused with Persian plans.
The Jama Masjids of Delhi and Ahmedabad display the mature style.

concepts.title: Colonial Architecture: Havelis to High Courts
concepts.definition: Colonial times added their own layer - merchant havelis of Shekhawati with frescoed courtyards, and grand public buildings such as the Madras High Court - where classical European facades adapted to Indian climate and craft.
concepts.key_idea: Colonial architecture grafted European styles onto Indian builders and settings.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees203.txt lines 79-95 (Madras High Court, Havelis of Shekhawati), 169-175
question_patterns: what are the havelis of Shekhawati famous for
describe the architecture of the Madras High Court
how did colonial buildings differ from traditional Indian ones
what materials and styles did colonial architecture use
why do havelis have frescoes and courtyards
give two examples of colonial public buildings in India

solution_steps.explain: Shekhawati havelis show merchant wealth in painted walls and planned courtyards.
Courts and offices copied European classical designs in brick and stone.
Verandas, thick walls and local craft softened the foreign style to Indian conditions.

concepts.title: Reading Monuments as Historical Sources
concepts.definition: Monuments are history written in stone: inscriptions, plans and styles reveal a building's patron, period, technology and religious life, so a journey through Indian architecture is a journey through India's past itself.
concepts.key_idea: Every pillar and inscription is a document - monuments testify about their times.
question_patterns: how do monuments help us study history
what can an inscription on a temple tell a historian
what does the plan of a building reveal about its purpose
how do architectural styles help date a monument
why should monuments be preserved
interpret a monument of your region as a historical source

solution_steps.explain: Inscriptions name donors, dates and deities.
Arch, dome or shikhara points to the period and culture.
Together, evidence from stones rebuilds the story of an age.
